page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r9i.6xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the KVM hypervisor. Compute is powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 6982P-C processors running at a base clock speed of 3.2 GHz across 24 dedicated vCPUs. The hardware platform delivers an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio, providing 192.0 GB of system memory, which translates to exactly 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

The instance does not include integrated local disk storage or hardware GPU acceleration, operating entirely diskless by default. All persistent storage and operational file systems must be provisioned through networked block storage volumes. External communication and data transfers are supported by a baseline network bandwidth allocation of 15 Gbps, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses included in the base profile.

From a cost efficiency standpoint, the high memory density allows organizations running memory-bound enterprise systems to scale capacity without paying for unneeded CPU cycles. However, the architectural tradeoff involves a complete reliance on network-attached storage, meaning heavy disk write operations will compete for network I/O unless dedicated storage throughput channels are factored into the deployment architecture.

Given its hardware allocation, Alibaba Cloud ecs.r9i.6xlarge is suited for in-memory database engines such as Redis and Memcached, large-scale relational databases, real-time analytics platforms, distributed cache tiers, and transactional enterprise workloads that demand substantial memory capacity per processing thread.
